turns.text: Empirical Case Study: Forensic Bioinformatics ([Baggerly & Coombes, 2009](#ref-baggerly2009)). Systems collapse when models mistake collection artifacts for real-world signals. In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
The Investigation: Duke University researchers published prominent papers claiming microarray expression patterns could predict patient chemotherapy response.
▸
The Forensic Audit: Statisticians Keith Baggerly and Kevin Coombes spent 1,500 hours forensically reconstructing the undocumented dataset. They discovered that gene labels had shifted down by one row in an Excel spreadsheet, reversing sensitive drug sensitivity classifications ((Baggerly & Coombes, 2009)).
⚡
The Aftermath: Because Duke lacked formal version control and data provenance logs, cancer patients received incorrect, toxic chemotherapy regimens. The scandal led to trial terminations, 10 retractions, and spurred the Institute of Medicine (IOM) to mandate immutable cryptographic versioning and open data dictionaries across clinical research.

solo.title: Empirical Case Study: Billion-Scale Multimodal Retrieval (Pinterest Visual Search)

In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:

The Retrieval Scale: Over $5\text{ Billion}$ visual pins are represented by 512-dimensional continuous feature embeddings.
▸
The Memory Challenge: Storing raw float32 vectors in GPU memory requires over $10.24\text{ Terabytes}$ of high-bandwidth VRAM, costing hundreds of thousands of dollars monthly.
